# Nestor (Mauricio) Collado

I am a PhD candidate in Environmental Economics at the Bren School of Environmental Science & Management at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

My research studies how regulators choose between prices, quantities, and bundled policy instruments when information is limited and ecosystems are complex. I work primarily in environmental and resource economics, with applications to fisheries, natural resources, and climate policy.

Across these settings, I am interested in how policy design changes when regulators cannot finely target behavior, species, or emissions, and how relatively coarse instruments can still improve environmental and economic outcomes under uncertainty.


**Job Market Paper:** [Bundle Fisheries Under Ecological Uncertainty](research.qmd) · [PDF](files/Collado_JMP_Bundle_Fisheries.pdf)

## Research Themes

### Environmental policy under limited information

I study how information constraints shape the choice between taxes, quotas, and broader policy bundles.

### Fisheries and natural resource economics

My work examines multispecies fisheries, extraction, and resource management under uncertainty.

### Dynamic modeling for policy design

I use dynamic economic models to understand regulation when ecosystems are complex and policy must remain feasible in practice.
